### Selected model and test evaluation

```{r selected-report-load, include=FALSE}
selected_root <- if (file.exists("outputs/selected_model/test_metrics.csv")) "." else ".."
selected_csv <- function(path) read.csv(file.path(selected_root, path), check.names = FALSE)

selection_cv     <- selected_csv("outputs/selected_model/comparison_summary.csv")
selected_metrics <- selected_csv("outputs/selected_model/test_metrics.csv")
selected_config  <- selected_csv("outputs/mlr_shared/mlr_selected_config.csv")

stopifnot(selection_cv$model[which.max(selection_cv$mean_macro_f1)] == "MLR (shared split)",
          selected_config$lambda == 0.001, selected_config$weights == "sqrt_inverse")

f4   <- function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x)
pct1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
pct2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * x)

selected_mlr <- selection_cv[selection_cv$model == "MLR (shared split)", ]
runner_up    <- selection_cv[order(-selection_cv$mean_macro_f1), ][2, ]
mlr_test     <- selected_metrics[selected_metrics$model == "MLR (shared split)", ]
base_test    <- selected_metrics[selected_metrics$model == "Majority baseline", ]
```

On the five shared provider-grouped folds, the corrected MLR retained the highest mean CV macro-F1 (**`r f4(selected_mlr$mean_macro_f1)`**, SD `r f4(selected_mlr$sd_macro_f1)`; mean accuracy `r pct2(selected_mlr$mean_accuracy)`), ahead of `r runner_up$model` (`r f4(runner_up$mean_macro_f1)`). This difference is descriptive and does not establish statistical superiority.

Before final evaluation, the original MLR functions and tuning grid were rerun with the shared split and five shared folds, because the original MLR split differed from the group's split. The corrected ridge multinomial model used alpha = 0, lambda = 0.001 and square-root inverse-frequency class weights. Its preprocessing and class weights were learned from the training data only, and it was refitted on all 13,497 training services. Model choice and parameters were fixed before test scores were computed, and the corrected model was not tuned on the test partition. However, the project's test partition had been exposed in earlier model work, so the results below are not a pristine independent confirmation and should be read as descriptive estimates.

```{r selected-report-test-table, echo=TRUE}
test_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Selected ridge MLR", "Majority-class baseline"),
  `Macro-F1` = f4(c(mlr_test$macro_f1, base_test$macro_f1)),
  Accuracy = pct2(c(mlr_test$accuracy, base_test$accuracy)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  test_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = paste0("Performance on the ", format(mlr_test$n_test, big.mark = ","),
                   "-service held-out test partition (not cross-validation).")
)
```

On the test partition, the selected MLR reached macro-F1 **`r f4(mlr_test$macro_f1)`** (mean CV macro-F1 `r f4(selected_mlr$mean_macro_f1)`), compared with `r f4(base_test$macro_f1)` for the majority-class baseline. Its accuracy was lower (`r pct2(mlr_test$accuracy)` against `r pct2(base_test$accuracy)`). This reflects the imbalance of the outcome: predicting Meeting NQS for every test service already gives `r pct2(base_test$accuracy)` accuracy. Higher accuracy alone would therefore not demonstrate useful performance across all tiers.

```{r selected-report-confusion, echo=TRUE}
test_cm <- selected_csv("outputs/selected_model/test_confusion_matrix.csv")
tiers <- c("Below NQS", "Meeting NQS", "Above NQS")
test_cm$Observed  <- factor(test_cm$Observed,  levels = tiers)
test_cm$Predicted <- factor(test_cm$Predicted, levels = tiers)
cm_table <- xtabs(Count ~ Observed + Predicted, data = test_cm)
knitr::kable(as.matrix(cm_table),
  caption = "MLR test-set confusion matrix: rows are actual tiers; columns are predicted tiers.")
```

```{r selected-report-recall, include=FALSE}
cm <- as.matrix(cm_table)
cm_recall <- diag(cm) / rowSums(cm)
```

Only **`r cm["Below NQS", "Below NQS"]` of `r sum(cm["Below NQS", ])` Below NQS services (`r pct1(cm_recall["Below NQS"])`)** were detected; `r cm["Below NQS", "Meeting NQS"]` were predicted as Meeting NQS and `r cm["Below NQS", "Above NQS"]` as Above NQS. Recall was `r pct1(cm_recall["Meeting NQS"])` for Meeting NQS and `r pct1(cm_recall["Above NQS"])` for Above NQS. Consequently, this model may inform exploratory review but should not be used alone to identify below-standard services or determine regulatory action.
